name: Judges

objectives.text: Identify Gideon, Deborah, and Samson as people God used to rescue Israel in the book of Judges
Name the judges as leaders God raised up for Israel in the time before Israel had kings
Retell how the people of Israel forgot God and how God sent a judge to save them when they cried out to him
Summarize the repeating cycle in Judges of sin, oppression, crying out, and deliverance
Explain how God gave Gideon victory over the Midianites with a small army so that Israel would know the victory came from the LORD
Describe the roles of Deborah, Barak, and Jael in Israel's deliverance from Sisera and the Canaanites
Compare the strength God gave Samson with his repeated disobedience and his broken Nazirite vow
Construct a chart of the major judges showing each judge's enemy, tribe or region, and years of rest
Explain how Israel's failure to drive out the Canaanites and its intermarriage with them led to idolatry
Analyze the refrain that in those days there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes
Explain what Judges means when it says the Spirit of the LORD came upon a judge to equip him for the task of deliverance
Interpret Jephthah's vow and its outcome in light of God's law about vows and child sacrifice
Connect Israel's moral decline to its religious compromise using the accounts of Micah's idol and the tribe of Dan
Analyze Gideon's refusal of kingship alongside his ephod and the rise of Abimelech to explain what Judges teaches about the LORD as Israel's true king
Explain how the LORD's compassion toward Israel in its distress shows his covenant faithfulness to an unfaithful people
Analyze how the judges grow progressively more flawed from Othniel to Samson and how this shapes the book's downward structure
Explain why Hebrews names Gideon, Barak, Samson, and Jephthah among examples of faith despite their failures
Evaluate the closing chapters of Judges, including the outrage at Gibeah and the civil war against Benjamin, as the climax of Israel's apostasy
Defend the Reformed teaching that God sovereignly accomplishes his purposes through flawed and sinful human instruments without being the author of their sin
Compose an essay tracing the spiral of apostasy in Judges and how the book's longing for a righteous king anticipates the kingship of Christ

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (characters, cycle, Gideon, Samson, refrain, Jephthah, decline and compromise, Spirit, chart, ending, sovereignty, essay). Turned the grade 3 feeling-free observation into a retelling objective at grade 2 tied to Judges 3:7-11. Merged categorizing enemies into the chart objective. Added Deborah and Jael, the incomplete conquest of Judges 1, Gideon's ephod and Abimelech on God as king, God's covenant compassion, the declining quality of the judges, and Hebrews 11 on flawed faith. Grounded the essay in a Christ-centered reading of the kingship theme. Added verse-specific anchors and confessional references only where they state the doctrine (vows, idolatry and images, providence, depravity, Christ as king).
